title: Windows CI for the Julia Pkg errors with 'Could not load symbol "duckdb_vector_size"'
body:
### What happens?

We have a failing Julia package build with DuckDB_jll 1.1.0 for Windows GitHub runners: https://github.com/TulipaEnergy/TulipaEnergyModel.jl/actions/runs/10833112611/job/30062514253

Revelant part reproduced:

```
ERROR: LoadError: could not load symbol "duckdb_vector_size":
The specified procedure could not be found. 
```

I saw other failures on 1.1.0, but I couldn't tell if they were related to this issue or not.

### To Reproduce

I created a simple repo building a Julia package that runs DuckDB here: https://github.com/reporter/DuckDBDebug.jl/actions/runs/10835456425/job/30067028887

You can see:
- It passes for ubuntu on DuckDB_jll 1.0.0 and 1.1.0
- It passes for Windows on DuckDB_jll 1.0.0
- It fails for Windows on DuckDB_jll 1.1.0

The code is very simple, and it doesn't actually run, since it fails on precompilation, but everything is included in the repo (https://github.com/reporter/DuckDBDebug.jl).

### OS:

windows-latest on CII

### DuckDB Version:

1.1.0

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Hi @reporter and @participant1, thanks for opening this issue and joining the discussion. The DuckDB Julia API is experimental and [not covered by community support](https://duckdblabs.com/news/2023/10/02/support-policy#apis). We welcome contributions fixing this issue but the core team is unlikely to fix this bug in the near future.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thanks for the reply @participant2. Just an update on our side, `DuckDB_jll@v1.1.0` is broken on local Windows machines as well, not just the CI.

Maybe limiting the `DuckDB` dependency on `DuckDB_jll` to `=1.0.0` is a workaround until it's fixed.

For other users, you can `add` and `pin` `DuckDB_jll` to `v1.0.0` with

```Julia-repl
pkg> add DuckDB_jll@v1.0.0
pkg> pin DuckDB_jll@v1.0.0
```

Since `DuckDB` compat bounds include `DuckDB_jll` 1.1.0, then you either do that or pin `DuckDB` itself to `v0.10.3`.

comments.author: GhostOfElectric
comments.body: If the 1.1.1 C/C++ windows library is downloaded from the DuckDB website and an environment variable  JULIA_DUCKDB_LIBRARY is set to point at duckdb.dll within it, then the latest version will successfully compile in Julia on windows.

<summary>The outline for a workflow `.github/workflows/JuliaRelease.yml` could be something like this:</summary>

```
name: On Tag

on:
  push:
    tags:        
      - 'v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+'

env:
  GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  update_duckdb:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Clone Yggdrasil
        run: git clone https://github.com/JuliaPackaging/Yggdrasil
    
      - name: Create branch
        run: |
          TAG=${{ github.ref }}
          BRANCH_NAME=update_duckdb_jll_${TAG#refs/tags/}
          git switch -c $BRANCH_NAME

      - name: Update version
        run: |
          COMMIT_HASH=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          sed -i "s|version = v\".*\"|version = v\"${TAG#refs/tags/}\"|g" D/DuckDB/build_tarballs.jl
          sed -i "s|GitSource(\"https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb.git\", \".*\")|GitSource(\"https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb.git\", \"$COMMIT_HASH\")|g" D/DuckDB/build_tarballs.jl

      - name: Commit changes
        run: |
          git add .
          git commit -m "Update DuckDB to commit $COMMIT_HASH"

      - name: Push changes
        run: git push --set-upstream origin $BRANCH_NAME

      - name: Create pull request
        run: gh pr create -B base_branch -H $BRANCH_NAME --title 'Merge $BRANCH_NAME into base_branch' --body 'Created by GitHub action'
```

</details>

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Looking at this a bit more - the compile commands issued are as follows:

```cpp
 /usr/bin/ccache /opt/bin/x86_64-w64-mingw32-libgfortran3-cxx11/x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++ 
--sysroot=/opt/x86_64-w64-mingw32/x86_64-w64-mingw32/sys-root/ 
-DDUCKDB_BUILD_LIBRARY -DDUCKDB_EXTENSION_AUTOINSTALL_DEFAULT=1 -DDUCKDB_EXTENSION_AUTOLOAD_DEFAULT=1 
-DEXT_VERSION_CORE_FUNCTIONS=\"v1.2.0\" -DEXT_VERSION_JSON=\"v1.2.0\" -DEXT_VERSION_PARQUET=\"v1.2.0\" 
@CMakeFiles/duckdb_fsst.dir/includes_CXX.rsp -O3 -DNDEBUG -O3 -DNDEBUG   -fvisibility=hidden
 -w -std=c++11 -MD -MT third_party/fsst/CMakeFiles/duckdb_fsst.dir/libfsst.cpp.obj -MF 
CMakeFiles/duckdb_fsst.dir/libfsst.cpp.obj.d -o CMakeFiles/duckdb_fsst.dir/libfsst.cpp.obj -c 
/workspace/srcdir/duckdb/third_party/fsst/libfsst.cpp
```

I'm guessing the `-fvisibility=hidden` is causing the symbols to be hidden.
In the `duckdb.h` header we normally explicitly label them for export on Windows which should circumvent this:

```cpp
#ifndef DUCKDB_API
#ifdef _WIN32
#ifdef DUCKDB_STATIC_BUILD
#define DUCKDB_API
#else
#if defined(DUCKDB_BUILD_LIBRARY) && !defined(DUCKDB_BUILD_LOADABLE_EXTENSION)
#define DUCKDB_API __declspec(dllexport)
#else
#define DUCKDB_API __declspec(dllimport)
#endif
#endif
#else
#define DUCKDB_API
#endif
#endif
```

Looking at the above definitions - this also seems like it should reach the part where `DUCKDB_API` is defined as `__declspec(dllexport)`:

* `DUCKDB_API` is not defined
* `DUCKDB_STATIC_BUILD` is not defined
* `DUCKDB_BUILD_LIBRARY` is defined

The only unknown is whether or not `_WIN32` is defined. If it is not defined that could be the problem. If it is defined maybe the `__declspec` is not being correctly handled by MinGW.

Given that this worked in the past and we haven't changed anything on our end here in a long time - my guess is that something has changed on the Julia build side of things. Perhaps they did not include `-fvisibility=hidden` by default before. We do not change this setting in DuckDB's CMake. The easiest solution would be to revert to not including this setting in the build. Perhaps there's an option in the `BinaryBuilders` script somewhere?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant11, the discussion and suggestions are about fixing the issue for the package. There are some comments in the beginning to bypass whe error using an earlier version. For instsance, you can do the following:

```julia-repl
julia> # Press the ] key to enter pkg mode
pkg> add DuckDB_jll@v1.0.0
pkg> pin DuckDB_jll@v1.0.0
pkg> # if DuckDB was already loaded, close and reopen julia
```

(from post https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/13911#issuecomment-2349252466), or, if you have a Project.toml, add something like in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/13911#issuecomment-2363836767.
You can check one example on our repo: https://github.com/TulipaEnergy/TulipaEnergyModel.jl/blob/d7cba2aad8bbda2aa0cca0bbc36c99b36fc409ea/Project.toml#L27

> Given that this worked in the past and we haven't changed anything on our end here in a long time - my guess is that something has changed on the Julia build side of things. Perhaps they did not include `-fvisibility=hidden` by default before. We do not change this setting in DuckDB's CMake. The easiest solution would be to revert to not including this setting in the build. Perhaps there's an option in the `BinaryBuilders` script somewhere?

I replicated the problem outside of `BinaryBuilder` (that's how I could bisect).  This is how I built it:
```shell
cmake -B build \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=mingw-w64-x86_64.cmake \
      -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS='autocomplete;icu;parquet;json;fts;tpcds;tpch' \
      -DENABLE_EXTENSION_AUTOLOADING=1 \
      -DENABLE_EXTENSION_AUTOINSTALL=1 \

      -DDUCKDB_EXPLICIT_PLATFORM=x86_64-w64-mingw32-cxx11 .
cmake --build build
```

I used [this toolchain file](https://gist.github.com/peterspackman/8cf73f7f12ba270aa8192d6911972fe8/).

I also downloaded the build logs from older working `DuckDB_jll` windows [releases](https://github.com/JuliaBinaryWrappers/DuckDB_jll.jl/releases), e.g. 1.0.0+3, and it includes `-fvisibility=hidden`.  So maybe that is not the issue.
